nodes.title: NOTICE
nodes.summary: This notice announces Kotak Mahindra Bank's 40th AGM on August 2, 2025, via video conferencing. Ordinary business includes adopting standalone and consolidated audited financial statements for FY 2024-25, declaring a dividend of ₹2.50 per equity share, reappointing Ms. Shanti Ekambaram as Director and Deputy Managing Director until October 31, 2025, and reappointing Mr. Ashok Vaswani as Director. It also covers appointing M M Nissim & Co LLP as Joint Statutory Auditors for FY 2025-26 to 2027-28 and fixing their remuneration up to ₹5 crore for FY 2025-26. Special business includes appointing Mr. Paritosh Kashyap as Whole-time Director (Executive Director) for three years and approving his remuneration.

It covers the statement under Section 102, quorum, NSDL's VC facility, member login procedures, document inspection, SEBI mandates for PAN, KYC, and nomination, dematerialization requirements, and e-mail communication of notices. It provides instructions for attending the AGM via VC, speaker registration, submitting questions, remote e-voting dates and eligibility, and procedures for e-voting and login for different member categories.

nodes.title: I. INFORMATION AND INSTRUCTIONS FOR E-VOTING BY INDIVIDUAL MEMBERS HOLDING EQUITY SHARES OF THE BANK IN DEMAT MODE

As per circular of SEBI on e-voting facility provided by listed entities dated 9th December, 2020, all individual members holding Equity Shares of the Bank in demat mode can cast their vote, by way of a single login credential, through their demat accounts / websites of Depositories / DPs. The procedure to login and access e-voting, as implemented by the Depositories / DPs is, given below:

nodes.summary: The text provides instructions for e-voting by institutional/corporate members and members holding physical shares. It requires institutional members to send board resolution/authority letter with attested signatures to the Scrutiniser via email. For members receiving an email from the Bank/NSDL, it outlines steps to access the NSDL e-voting website, login using User ID (based on Demat NSDL, CDSL, or physical folio), and password details. It explains retrieving initial password, resetting forgotten passwords, OTP-based login, and accepting terms before casting votes. It also covers processes for members whose email is not registered.

nodes.title: STEP 2: CAST YOUR VOTE ELECTRONICALLY ON NSDL E-VOTING SYSTEM
nodes.summary: The section guides shareholders through electronic voting on the NSDL e-voting system, including login, selecting the EVEN, casting and confirming votes, and printing the vote confirmation. It provides general guidelines for institutional and corporate members on submitting board resolutions and authority letters, password management, account lockout, obtaining login credentials, and voting rights based on the cut-off date (26th July 2025). It also covers the appointment of scrutinizer, submission of the scrutiny report, and announcement of results by 5th August 2025. Dividend-related information includes the record date (18 July 2025), payment date (on or before 8 August 2025), instructions for updating details, claiming unclaimed dividends, and tax implications with documentation requirements for nil/lower TDS and DTAA benefits, with a submission deadline of 22 July 2025. Finally, it requests shareholders to update PAN, email, bank, and other details via depositories or RTA by July 18, 2025, and references an Explanatory Statement under the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI Regulation 17(11).

nodes.title: General Guidelines for members
nodes.summary: The text outlines guidelines for institutional/corporate members to submit board resolutions and authority letters for e-voting, either via email or upload, with attested signatures. It stresses password confidentiality and account lockout after five failed attempts, with reset options. Contact details for queries are provided. For members without registered email, steps to obtain login credentials are detailed, including required documents for physical and demat holdings. It references FAQs and manuals for grievances, specifies voting rights proportional to shareholding as of the cut-off date (26th July 2025), and notes non-members should treat the notice as informational. It announces the appointment of scrutinizer and alternate scrutinizer, the submission of the scrutiny report, and the announcement of results by 5th August 2025. Finally, it states that results and the scrutinizer's report will be posted on the Bank's and NSDL's websites, displayed at the registered office, and forwarded to stock exchanges.

nodes.title: 24. Dividend-Related Information:
nodes.summary: The text details dividend-related information, including the record date (18 July 2025) for determining eligible members, and the payment date (on or before 8 August 2025). It instructs dematerialised shareholders to update address/bank details with DPs before the record date, and urges members to claim unclaimed dividends to avoid transfer to the IEPF Authority, specifically for FY 2017-18. It outlines tax implications: dividends are taxable in members' hands, with TDS at 10% for residents with valid PAN (20% without), and exemptions for low dividend income (<₹10,000) or valid Form 15G/15H. It lists documents required for nil/lower TDS for specific resident entities (insurers, mutual funds, AIFs, NPS Trust, others) and for non-residents to avail DTAA benefits (PAN, TRC, Form 10F, etc.). It sets a deadline (22 July 2025) for submitting documents and notes the Bank's right to recover demands due to incorrect information.

nodes.title: Updation of PAN, e-mail address, Bank account and other details:
nodes.summary: The text requests shareholders to update PAN, email, bank, and other details: dematerialised holders via Depositories/DPs; physical holders via Form ISR-1 to KFIN with supporting self-attested documents (cancelled cheque/passbook and PAN card) by July 18, 2025, or upload at ris.kfintech.com/form15. It notes TDS deduction based on RTA records with no revision requests, allows certain non-individual members to submit through NSDL-registered custodians, provides Kotak's Investor Relations site for downloads, states no tax determination communication after the deadline, mentions refund option for higher TDS, disclaims Bank liability, and references email communication. It also introduces an Explanatory Statement under Section 102(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI Regulation 17(11) covering Item Nos. 4 and 6 to 10 of the Notice dated June 28, 2025.

nodes.title: ITEM NO. 4
nodes.summary: The text details Ms. Shanti Ekambaram's appointment as Director and Whole-time Director of the Bank effective 1st November 2022, following RBI approval, for a term up to 31st October 2025. It notes her re-designation as Deputy Managing Director from 19th March 2024 and her decision to retire upon completion of her term on 31st October 2025, accepted by the Board on 31st May 2025. It mentions that brief details of Ms. Ekambaram are provided in the Annexure as per SEBI Listing Regulations and SS-2. Pursuant to Section 152 of the Companies Act, she retires by rotation at the Fortieth Annual General Meeting and offers herself for re-appointment until the end of her current term. The Board recommends an Ordinary Resolution at Item No. 4, and it states that Ms. Ekambaram and her relatives may be deemed concerned or interested, while no other Directors, Key Managerial Personnel, or their relatives are concerned or interested in the resolution.

nodes.title: ITEM NOS. 6 AND 7
nodes.summary: This text details the appointment of Joint Statutory Auditors for a bank. It notes Deloitte Haskins & Sells' appointment for FY2024-25 to FY2026-27 and KKC & Associates LLP's term expiring at the ensuing AGM. To replace KKC, the Board recommends M M Nissim & Co LLP as Joint Statutory Auditor for FY2025-26 to FY2027-28, subject to member approval. The text covers M M Nissim's credentials, RBI approval, and proposed remuneration not exceeding ₹5 crore for FY2025-26. It seeks member approval for the appointment, remuneration, and authorization to the Board to finalize terms, including role allocation and remuneration adjustments. It also states that none of the directors or key managerial personnel are interested in the resolutions.

nodes.title: ITEM NO. 8
nodes.summary: The text details the Board's appointment of Mr. Paritosh Kashyap as an Additional Director and Whole-time Director (Executive Director) for three years, pending regulatory approvals, following Ms. Shanti Ekambaram's retirement. It outlines his qualifications, extensive experience in banking and financial services, and current role as Group President and Business Head – Wholesale Banking Group. The appointment is based on NRC recommendation, RBI 'Fit and Proper' criteria, and compliance with applicable laws. It covers his expertise, Board's rationale, member approval sought via Ordinary Resolution, and confirmation that he is not related to any Director or KMP, with no other directors interested except him and his relatives.

nodes.title: ITEM NO. 9
nodes.summary: The Board approved the appointment of M/s. Parikh & Associates as Secretarial Auditor for five years (FY 2025-26 to FY 2029-30), subject to member approval, pursuant to SEBI Listing Regulations and Companies Act provisions. The firm's credentials are detailed: established in 1987, peer-reviewed, with diverse client base and expertise in corporate law, SEBI regulations, and FEMA compliance. The firm confirmed valid peer review, no disqualifications, no conflict of interest, and consent to appointment within ICSI limits. Proposed remuneration for FY 2025-26 is up to ₹500,000 plus expenses, with future revisions by the Board. The Board recommends an Ordinary Resolution, and no directors or key managerial personnel are interested.

nodes.title: ITEM NO. 10
key_items: a. Name of the related party: Mr. Jay Kotak
nodes.summary: The text outlines Section 188 of the Companies Act, 2013, and related rules regarding related party transactions, specifically for a bank. It details the approval process for appointing a related party to an office or place of profit, including Board, member, and Audit Committee approvals, and exemptions for arm's length transactions. It then focuses on Mr. Jay Kotak, son of Director Uday Kotak, summarizing his qualifications, career history within the Kotak Group, and past approvals for his remuneration. It presents his current remuneration, performance ratings, and a proposal to increase his remuneration limit from ₹6,000,000 to ₹10,000,000 per annum due to his performance and qualifications. It includes disclosures under Rule 15 of the MBP Rules, the rationale for seeking member approval as good governance, and the Board's recommendation for an Ordinary Resolution, noting voting restrictions for related parties.

nodes.title: DETAILS OF THE DIRECTORS AS SET OUT IN THE NOTICE

It includes each director's name, DIN, age, qualifications, expertise, terms of appointment, remuneration sought and last drawn, appointment dates, directorships and committee positions in other entities, resignations from listed entities in the past three years, relationships with other directors/KMP, and shareholding in the Bank. The section also covers board meeting attendance for FY 2024-25 and committee memberships/chairmanships in the Bank for each director, with Kashyap's marked not applicable. Additionally, it includes an authorization by the Company Secretary and details about the 40th Annual General Meeting (AGM) scheduled for August 2, 2025, via video conferencing, along with QR codes and web links for the AGM Notice and Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 due to unregistered email addresses, important dates for e-voting, and encouragement for members to update email and KYC details.
